# /rite:delete — remove an item that should not exist

Arguments: `$ARGUMENTS`

Deleting is for mistakes: a duplicate, an item created in the wrong cycle or from a misread plan.
Giving work up is not deleting — a task is `rite mark <ID> skipped --reason "…" --commit`, a fix
`rite mark-stale` — because both keep the record. Only an item never worked on (`pending`,
`blocked`, `skipped`, no `done_commit`) can go; its ID stays under `deleted` and is never handed out
again.

## Steps

1. `rite delete <ID> --dry-run [--detach] --json` per ID. `eligible: false` → report its
   `blockers` and the way out, and leave it:
   - started or done → give it up instead (skipped / stale), as the message says;
   - a fix with it as `origin` → that fix must go first (delete it too, if it is also a mistake);
   - another item's `depends_on` → `--detach` drops it there; say which items lose the dependency;
   - a link in a document (`path:line`) → the user rewrites that prose; never edit it to unblock.
2. **Confirm every deletion** with AskUserQuestion: each eligible item with its title and status,
   what `--detach` releases (`detach`) and whether it leaves the cycle's `order`. Ask for the reason in
   the same round when the arguments give none. A deletion is never assumed — not with `--yes`, not
   when questions cannot be asked: then report the dry run and stop.
3. For each confirmed ID, fixes before the tasks they came from: `rite delete <ID> --reason "<reason>"
   [--detach] --json`. One commit per item (`chore(rite): delete <ID> (<reason>)`) carrying the
   removed file, the JSON and the views; in a local cycle it writes the files and commits nothing.
4. `rite check --quick --cycle <cycle> --json`.

## Report

Per ID: deleted (commit SHA, or "local cycle") or refused (blockers, way out) · dependencies dropped
by `--detach` · what to run next.

## The CLI

Every state read and every state change goes through it: hand-written bookkeeping drifts.

```sh
sh "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/bin/rite" <subcommand> [args] --json
```

Find it in that order, never by searching the disk: `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/bin/rite`,
`$RITE_HOME/bin/rite`, `rite` on `PATH`; none → ask the user. Below, `rite <sub>` means that
invocation, run inside the repository or with `--root <repo>`; prefer `--json`.

Exit codes: `0` ok · `1` failure or nothing selected (stderr names the rule; no `--force` unless
asked) · `3` no `rite.toml` — stop and tell the user to run `/rite:init`.

Reply in the JSON's `session_language`; empty → the session's language.

## State

The cycle's `progress.json` (meta + tasks) and `fixes.json` are the only state; item files hold prose
and their `id`; the tables in the progress and fixes files are views the CLI renders from the JSON.

- `rite begin <kind> [--cycle C] [--id ID] --json` resolves the cycle, takes the item and returns its
  paths, the config digest and the commit template. Idempotent.
- `rite finish <ID> [--sha S] --json` closes the item from its work commit, runs `check --quick` and
  names the next one. Two commits per item — the work, then the CLI's record (a commit cannot hold its
  own SHA). No work commit, only a document outside git: `--no-repo --reason "…"`, never borrow HEAD.
- Others: `rite mark <ID> blocked|skipped --reason "…" --commit`, `mark-reviewed <ID> [--fixes …]`,
  `mark-stale <FIX> --reason "…"`, `rebind <ID> --sha <commit>` after a squash.
- A fix blocked by the environment adds `--unblocked-by "<command that passes once it is there>"`.
  Partial work: commit what is coherent, then `mark blocked` with the `--reason` naming what is
  missing and the partial SHA — never `close` (not done), never `mark-stale` (the symptom is there).
- A **local cycle** (`"local": true`) writes the same fields and commits nothing, by design; never
  commit its documents yourself.

- Planning fields: `rite set <ID> --files a,b --resources r --depends-on <IDs>`; the cycle's `order`,
  `ticket`, `plan`: `rite set-cycle --cycle C --order <IDs>`. The only fields you write.

Never edit `progress.json` / `fixes.json` (the guard refuses it), never put fields back into an item's
frontmatter, never edit between `<!-- rite:begin … -->` and `<!-- rite:end -->`, never invent an ID.

## Asking the user

Ask only what the repository cannot answer, in one round, with AskUserQuestion (at most 4 questions,
recommended option first). Every question is a context switch; guesses the commands then obey are worse.

With `--yes` in the arguments (or when questions cannot be asked): do not ask. Take the recommended
option of each and list them in the report as `assumed: <question> → <choice>`. Even then, never choose
an option that deletes, moves or overwrites existing files, and never apply retro proposals — write
them down only.

## Reporting

**At most 15 lines.** IDs, commands, measured numbers, SHAs, and what the user must decide. Do not
re-tell what the item file already says, and do not paste output that was not decisive.
